note: Two courts and two first-round matchUps: the first Garman slot holds one matchUp per court, so both start at the venue opening.

One court, T = 90, L = 30. Periods number from 0 at the opening (period 0 totals C, period 1 adds none, as Brian Garman's published tables do), and each total is rounded to the nearest match: 1, 1, 1.33 → 1, 1.67 → 2, so the second matchUp starts at 11:30, when the first is expected to end (scheduling-pipeline.md § 9.6, decided).

Both semifinals at 10:00 on two courts; their players are free at 10:00 + 90 + 60 = 12:30, so the final, profiled the same day, takes the first slot at or after 12:30, which is 12:30 (two courts: 10:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 12:30, ...).

A DO_NOT_SCHEDULE request from 10:00 to 11:30 for a participant placed in the matchUp: a 90 minute matchUp overlaps it from any start before 11:30, so the 10:00 slot is refused and the matchUp takes the court's next slot, 11:30.
A daily limit of one singles matchUp: every finalist is already booked for a semifinal on the date, so the final is over the limit and reported as such, never timed.
The venue's only court is disabled on the date: there are no slots, and every profiled matchUp is reported without a time.

Both semifinals were played on day 2 and the final is profiled on day 1: every slot on day 1 is before its played sources, so the final is held back under the played order and not reported as merely untimed.
